stem_note: Shared stems ("For the following exercises...") are copied into each governed exercise's self-contained text; where a stem cites a numbered book equation or a printed table, that content is inlined with a one-line disclosure in the exercise's notes field. \(P(x)\) denotes the population of a city at time \(x\) in years. Describe what the following two expressions represent in this context, including units: (a) \((P(x + h) - P(x)) / h\), and (b) \(P'(x) = lim_{h -> 0} (P(x + h) - P(x)) / h\).
exercises.notes: The shared stem's two general expressions ((f(x+h)-f(x))/h and f'(x) = lim_{h to 0} (f(x+h)-f(x))/h) are inlined here in terms of P per the shared stem citing them.

exercises.text: Sketch the graph of a function \(y = f(x)\) with all of the following properties: (a) \(f'(x) > 0\) for \(-2 <= x < 1\); (b) \(f'(2) = 0\); (c) \(f'(x) > 0\) for \(x > 2\); (d) \(f(2) = 2\) and \(f(0) = 1\); (e) \(lim_{x -> -infinity} f(x) = 0\) and \(lim_{x -> infinity} f(x) = infinity\); (f) \(f'(1)\) does not exist.

Suppose temperature \(T\) in degrees Fahrenheit at a height \(x\) feet above the ground is given by \(y = T(x)\). (a) Give a physical interpretation, with units, of \(T'(x)\). (b) If we know that \(T'(1000) = -0.1\), explain the physical meaning.

Suppose the total profit of a company is \(y = P(x)\) thousand dollars when \(x\) units of an item are sold. (a) What does \((P(b) - P(a)) / (b - a)\) for \(0 < a < b\) measure, and what are the units? (b) What does \(P'(x)\) measure, and what are the units? (c) Suppose that \(P'(30) = 5\), what is the approximate change in profit if the number of items sold increases from 30 to 31?

The graph in the following figure models the number of people \(N(t)\) who have come down with the flu \(t\) weeks after its initial outbreak in a town with a population of 50,000 citizens. (a) Describe what \(N'(t)\) represents and how it behaves as \(t\) increases. (b) What does the derivative tell us about how this town is affected by the flu outbreak?

The following table shows the height \(h\) (in meters) of the Saturn V rocket for the Apollo 11 mission at time \(t\) (in seconds) after launch: \(t = 0\) s, \(h = 0\) m; \(t = 1\) s, \(h = 2\) m; \(t = 2\) s, \(h = 4\) m; \(t = 3\) s, \(h = 13\) m; \(t = 4\) s, \(h = 25\) m; \(t = 5\) s, \(h = 32\) m. What is the physical meaning of \(h'(t)\)? What are the units?

exercises.text: [T] Using the table showing the height \(h\) (in meters) of the Saturn V rocket for the Apollo 11 mission at time \(t\) (in seconds) after launch (\(t = 0\) s, \(h = 0\) m; \(t = 1\) s, \(h = 2\) m; \(t = 2\) s, \(h = 4\) m; \(t = 3\) s, \(h = 13\) m; \(t = 4\) s, \(h = 25\) m; \(t = 5\) s, \(h = 32\) m), construct a table of values for \(h'(t)\) and graph both \(h(t)\) and \(h'(t)\) on the same graph. (Hint: for interior points, estimate both the left limit and the right limit and average them. An interior point of an interval \(I\) is an element of \(I\) that is not an endpoint of \(I\).)
exercises.notes: The shared stem's Saturn V height-vs-time table is inlined here per the stem governing exercises 100-105.

exercises.text: [T] Using the table showing the height \(h\) (in meters) of the Saturn V rocket for the Apollo 11 mission at time \(t\) (in seconds) after launch (\(t = 0\) s, \(h = 0\) m; \(t = 1\) s, \(h = 2\) m; \(t = 2\) s, \(h = 4\) m; \(t = 3\) s, \(h = 13\) m; \(t = 4\) s, \(h = 25\) m; \(t = 5\) s, \(h = 32\) m): the best linear fit to the data is given by \(H(t) = 7.229t - 4.905\), where \(H\) is the height of the rocket (in meters) and \(t\) is the time elapsed since takeoff. From this equation, determine \(H'(t)\). Graph \(H(t)\) with the given data and, on a separate coordinate plane, graph \(H'(t)\).

exercises.text: [T] Using the table showing the height \(h\) (in meters) of the Saturn V rocket for the Apollo 11 mission at time \(t\) (in seconds) after launch (\(t = 0\) s, \(h = 0\) m; \(t = 1\) s, \(h = 2\) m; \(t = 2\) s, \(h = 4\) m; \(t = 3\) s, \(h = 13\) m; \(t = 4\) s, \(h = 25\) m; \(t = 5\) s, \(h = 32\) m): the best quadratic fit to the data is given by \(G(t) = 1.429t^2 + 0.0857t - 0.1429\), where \(G\) is the height of the rocket (in meters) and \(t\) is the time elapsed since takeoff. From this equation, determine \(G'(t)\). Graph \(G(t)\) with the given data and, on a separate coordinate plane, graph \(G'(t)\).

exercises.text: [T] Using the table showing the height \(h\) (in meters) of the Saturn V rocket for the Apollo 11 mission at time \(t\) (in seconds) after launch (\(t = 0\) s, \(h = 0\) m; \(t = 1\) s, \(h = 2\) m; \(t = 2\) s, \(h = 4\) m; \(t = 3\) s, \(h = 13\) m; \(t = 4\) s, \(h = 25\) m; \(t = 5\) s, \(h = 32\) m): the best cubic fit to the data is given by \(F(t) = 0.2037t^3 + 2.956t^2 - 2.705t + 0.4683\), where \(F\) is the height of the rocket (in meters) and \(t\) is the time elapsed since takeoff. From this equation, determine \(F'(t)\). Graph \(F(t)\) with the given data and, on a separate coordinate plane, graph \(F'(t)\). Does the linear, quadratic, or cubic function fit the data best?

exercises.text: Using the best linear, quadratic, and cubic fits to the Saturn V rocket height data (\(H(t) = 7.229t - 4.905\), \(G(t) = 1.429t^2 + 0.0857t - 0.1429\), and \(F(t) = 0.2037t^3 + 2.956t^2 - 2.705t + 0.4683\), where \(t\) is the time in seconds elapsed since takeoff), determine what \(H''(t)\), \(G''(t)\), and \(F''(t)\) are. What are the physical meanings of \(H''(t)\), \(G''(t)\), and \(F''(t)\), and what are their units?
